chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Ibn Abi Umeyr from Jameel ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
There is no problem with a man giving on behalf of his dependents while they are absent from him, and with his instructing them so that they give on his behalf while he is absent from them.
ai.seo_question: Can a man pay Zakat on behalf of his family if they are not present?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the flexibility in Islamic jurisprudence regarding the fulfillment of financial obligations, specifically highlighting the validity of vicarious payment (wakalah) within family structures. It reflects the practical legal reasoning of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in accommodating the realities of absence, ensuring that religious duties like Zakat are not hindered by physical separation between the head of household and his dependents. This principle reinforces the concept of collective familial responsibility while maintaining individual accountability through proper authorization.
